snapshot.date: 4 am Faoilleach, AE 1 (the eve of the Crossing)
snapshot.plan_label: LE 1,819 (ERA_PLAN): the close of the Landfall Era; the snapshot is the day before the humans come ashore
snapshot.description: Eighteen centuries after the fleet of the willing sailed north-about into Manannan's mist, the island is one realm with an empty crown. The Council of Custodians sits at Cathair dhearg in the crown's place, for the ruler of Dia-thìr has been master of the vein-house too since Dòmhnall Ruadh, and the heads of the seven houses of custody are the council; the kingdom seals with the vein-house's trellis and hollow stone. The shires keep the firlot of Cathair dhearg and their seats keep the crown's measures; the coal-roads from the mountain are the crown's, posted and ridden. The Small-Burning Law still holds, though three of the seven houses now hold more than half the right, and the silver petition lies unanswered. The orders of the Old Faith have their houses: the Hawk at Cnoc bheag, the Stone at Inis thais, Manannan at Seann Skell, Macha with the crown, the schools arguing at Dùn thais; the Old Spirits keep the spirit-house at Dùn ìseal. The north-west is thinly held since the dearth. On the north-west the mist lies thinner each winter, and on still mornings the fishers see the line of the open sea.

land_changes.what: Manannan's mist lies on the eastern sea beyond the northern and eastern headlands (from the Setting-Out, LE 40), thinning in the last years; draw as a sea zone, not a coast change.
The oak grove that named Doire fhionn is gone, felled for the keels of the fleet (LE 5); the northern Doire shires cut their woods by coppice.
The Abhainn bheag below Ros fhionn is silted by a shifting bar (LE 1,159); the salt barges cannot reach its quays.
The salt pans of Caol gharbh are under the sea (LE 1,734).

polities.name: Dia-thìr
polities.name_en: the realm of Dia-thìr (the crown empty; the Council of Custodians in its place)
polities.form: a crown joined to the custody of the vein (from LE 859); the crown empty at the close of the age, and the Council of Custodians, the heads of the seven houses, sitting in its place

ruler.title: the Council of Custodians (high custodian Tormod mac Ailein, first named in AE 2)
ruler.note: The last crowning in the annals is Gormshuil nic Thormoid's (LE 1,766); of her death, any heir and how the crown fell vacant nothing is told. Tormod mac Ailein is high custodian when the council grants the strangers leave; that he already sits at the snapshot is inferred.

admin_units.kind: shire: the unit in which the crown's measures are kept; a year's grain at every seat under Iain Ciar
admin_units.note: The word siorrachd first appears at the sail-cloth levy (LE 9). The modern shires whose seats stand in this age are used; Doire chaol is folded back into Baile chiar and the two island shires into their nearest neighbours.

units.note: the first king chosen by the houses; the double court at Baile Mòr dhomhain

units.name: Clann Ìomhair
units.note: walled Dùn dhearg in stone, the first walls raised by a house

units.name: Clann Raghnaill
units.note: the claimant slain at Muileann chrom; from Dòmhnall Ruadh the crown and the vein-house together

units.note: no deed set down under its name in this age

units.note: rebuilt the bath-house at the hot springs; brought the silver petitions

units.name: Clann Lachlainn

units.name_en: Seann Warr, keeper of its own gates and tolls

diplomacy.relation: none: no word since the broken tidings of two landfalls
diplomacy.note: Queen Beathag struck her sister Mòrag's line from the succession as no longer on Dia-thìr; Manannan's order prays that the sea be kept shut.

cultures.name: Na Dia-thìrich
cultures.note: One people; nearly one household in five of the coal-right went with the fleet. The departed are beyond the mist and hold no land here.

faiths.name: An Creideamh Sean
faiths.name_en: the Old Faith and its orders
faiths.deity: an Dagda first; each order its own god

orders.name: Òrd Bhrìde
orders.name_en: the custody of the vein (the vein-house: Crom's stone, heir to the Keepers' Hall)
orders.gods: Brìde of the flame; Crom Cruaich of the stone
orders.note: The vein-house above Muileann dhearg keeps Crom's stone and the custody-book and holds the Small-Burning Law; since LE 859 the ruler is its master. It has no written creed.

orders.name: Òrd an t-Seabhaig
orders.name_en: the order of the Hawk of Acaill (the Hungry Hawk)
orders.gods: Mòd, the Hawk of Acaill; Fionntan mac Bòchra
orders.note: Gathered at Cnoc bheag by Gormshuil nic Artair (LE 229); split in LE 889, the Fed Hawk turned out to the northern Seann Skell and not heard of as a house after its petition was refused.

orders.name: Scoiltean nan Draoidhean
orders.gods: Flidais, lady of the deer; the white stag
orders.note: Houses of disputation at Dùn thais (LE 314, shut and opened more than once) and Inis mhòr (LE 769); they keep Coille Naomh Muileann chiar and walk its bounds; Eilidh Dhubh's tracts burned; the table of years forbidden.

orders.name: Òrd Mhacha
orders.name_en: the order of Macha, the order of the crown
orders.gods: Macha; Liath Macha and Dubh Sainglenn, two horses, one yoke
orders.note: The order of Cathair dhearg and the crown since King Aonghas (LE 441); keeper of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag by royal grant; its great house at Cathair mhòr.

orders.name: Òrd na Cloiche
orders.name_en: the order of the Stone (Lia Fàil) and its Fianna
orders.note: First preached at Inis thais (LE 409), its temple roofed with northern slate; split over prayer for the dead (LE 1,389): the temple at Inis thais and the house at Baile gheal, not reconciled.

orders.name: Òrd Mhanannain
orders.gods: Manannan mac Lir; the yellow scorpion of his Cup of Truth
orders.note: Proclaimed at Seann Skell (LE 654); no boat of the faithful out of sight of land; the prayer to keep the sea shut, said on the day of the empty-harbour rite; it records the mist thinning.

faiths.name: Na Seann Spioradan
faiths.note: The spirit-house at Dùn ìseal with the names of the dead of the eastern shires on wooden posts, cut anew each generation; the guest-house at Allt an Àigh; the ancestor shrine and feast-market at Seann Tarr.

routes.rule: A master trail or sea-lane is present when every town it touches stands in this age (or both end towns stand and at most a quarter between are not yet towns); lanes touching no town are kept. The crown's coal-roads and the queen's road are roads; the lanes the annals date later are absent. The cold way of the northern grain barges (route 383) was laid up in LE 1,634 and is absent.

new.note: forty-one barges counted at the bridge carrying the fleet's grain to the capital, on by the coast to Ros àrsaidh and up the Abhainn naomh to Seann Skell

master.note: Rebuilt in dressed stone by Clann Choinnich; the sick of any house admitted one day in seven.
The Old Spirits renew the pilgrimage and build a guest-house beside the stream.
Neck-rings for the heads of the seven houses; the silver fellowship keeps its craft within four families. Twice Clann Choinnich asked to smelt it with the coal, and was refused.
Widened for two carts; Queen Sìleas's name cut on the downstream parapet.
Built anew at the salt-masters' cost with their names on the keystones; fallen quiet since the salt went by sea, and the office of bridge-keeper done away with.
Rebuilt in stone by Eilidh nic Chaluim, already known for its jugged buffalo; the queen's road runs past it.
Feeds the queen's progress with pan-fried spinach and black wine.
Oatcakes fried in linseed oil and fire water for the coal-carters; its keeper fined for watering the fire water.
Snowed in a whole season with a party of custodians' reeves inside.
Syrupped beef for the custodians' reeves on their rounds.
Where the ox-teams wait out the snow; the brothers made their peace under its roof.
Chartered with the seven great road-houses; the keepers settle their accounts here each year.

master.era_name_en: the fire on the Baile chrom headland
master.note: A driftwood fire over the thinned north-western coast.
A driftwood and seal-fat fire.
A driftwood fire kept by fisher-families.
The way in toward Seann Tarr, whose harbour is gone.

master.era_name_en: the stone tower at Tobar dhearg
master.note: The first sea-light raised above the ground; the village below roofed in slate after its fire.

master.era_name_en: the field of the Brothers' War below Muileann ghlas
master.note: Iain Ciar defeated Alasdair Bàn here and took him alive (LE 1,274).
Quarrymen broke into it and found a stair going down beyond their lamps; the custodians walled it up. The one who went down never told.
Found again by charcoal-burners, with the same cut stair; walled up, and its entry bound in the custody-book to the other's.
Seen near enough to foul the nets of the thinned north-west coast.
The shepherds light no fires on the high pastures and at last forsake them; a reeve sent to make them see sense does not stay the night.
Kept by the druids of the schools, who walk its bounds each year: the one open rite of the schools.
Its custody passed by royal grant to the priests of Macha; the other claimants left without contest.
Boats out of the small islands rob the coasting traders; a force of Queen Eilidh Bhàn burned their boats on Eilean dhubh and hanged Uilleam Ruadh.
The raiders' islets of the east (no raid recorded in this age).
The north-western strands, thinly held since the dearth.
The priests of the Hawk cleared its moss and tried to read it, and wrote down that they tried.
Cuimhnich an teine.
The column of the saying.
Measured into Ailean mac Dhùghaill's tables of the old ruins.
Measured into Ailean mac Dhùghaill's tables.
Measured by Ailean mac Dhùghaill: the altar faces the central mountains and not the sea.

master.era_name_en: the loft of papers at Muileann chaol
master.note: Beathag nic Thòmais's loft over her mill, bought copies of the custody-book and the harbour rolls; the three copies of the landfall tidings side by side.

master.era_name_en: the old games-field of the road-guards
master.note: The stone-walled field at Ceann leathan (the games are not recorded in this age).

master.era_name_en: the harvest fair at Muileann òg
master.note: The merchants of the long city go to it as one company.
The ferry family's landing; the southern lane of the Caol fhiadhaich fishers ends here.
The crossing days kept by the southern shires in writing; the panther year of LE 1,729 kept flocks in folds from Cnoc àrsaidh to the coast.
The custodian houses bury their heads here among graves older than any name on them.
The headmen of Caol gharbh and Caol chrom settle the dues of the strait at the stone on the neck.
The meeting of the cups.
The Mason's Point.

new.name: Cidhe an Diosail
new.name_en: the quay of the sunwise turn
new.note: The west quay the fleet sailed from, lengthened in dressed stone; renamed so that trade might go on under the old name. The rite of the empty harbour and the prayer for the shut sea are kept here on one day.
Keeper of Crom's stone and the custody-book; the lot-stones for the galleries kept in a bag and shown to visitors; the seal of the trellis and the hollow stone.
The names of the dead of the eastern shires on posts cut anew each generation; burned by lightning and cut again from memory; cracked by the earthquake of LE 1,649.
The first temple to the Stone by name, roofed with slate brought by sea.
The largest roofed building of the age; its floor of black and white eleven years in the laying.

new.name_en: the house of the Hawk and the Book of the Hawk
new.note: Gormshuil nic Artair's first house; the Hungry Hawk kept it after the schism.
Dùghall Garbh broke Raghnall Ruadh's host; some three hundred dead, most drowned in the ford.
Taken after forty days when the dead of the siege lines fouled its wells; the garrison freed on oath.
Raghnall Ruadh fell here; his own custodians opened the vein-house the next day.
The battle that named the Brothers' War.

new.name_en: the stone of the fourteen names
new.note: At the mouth of the fallen gallery of Cill ghlas.

new.name_en: the salt pans of Ros fhionn
new.note: Brine springs on the river flats; Ros fhionn salt was the measure of worth in the north-east.
The first paper on Dia-thìr, made from rags; the custody-book first copied onto paper.
Queen Eilidh Bhàn's force burned the boats on the strand of Eilean dhubh.
The grant of its own gates and tolls cut over the landward gate.

new.name_en: the felled grove of Doire fhionn
new.note: Felled for the keels of the fleet and drawn to the coast on ox-sleds; it never grew again.

new.name_en: the house of disputation at Dùn thais
new.note: Carson an làmh seo? argued by rule; shut for a generation after the table of years.

new.name_en: the timber from beyond the mist
new.note: Longer than any tree on the island, with nails no smith knows; carried to Seann Skell and burned.

zones.name_en: Manannan's mist on the eastern sea
zones.sea: the open sea west of the western headlands
zones.note: Hides Dia-thìr from every ship beyond it since the fleet sailed into it; thinner each winter at the snapshot.

zones.name_en: the roll of the willing and the Setting-Out (LE 2–40)
zones.note: The willing entered on boards at Seann Skell by household; nearly one household in five of the coal-right went; nineteen hulls (or twenty-one).

zones.name_en: the cold hearths of the War of the Three Claimants (LE 558)
zones.note: Raghnall Ruadh, holding the vein-house, denied the handful to every hearth and temple in the shires that stood against him; which shires is not told, so all but his own country are drawn.

zones.name_en: the swallowing cough and the closed coast road (LE 1,079–1,082)
zones.note: From Muileann dhomhain along the coast road to Seann Bhral; the queen closed the road and set reeves at the fords.

zones.name_en: the dearth on the north-west shore (LE 819), thinly held since
zones.note: Harvest after harvest failed; families left for the inland shires and the east. A reeve later counted fewer households than berths.

zones.name_en: the tremors of Cill ghlas (LE 379; LE 929)
zones.note: Three wells cracked; later a gallery fell and killed fourteen.

zones.name_en: the dry years at Achadh shean (LE 1,479)
zones.note: Three dry seasons; the crown carted grain in from the south; the wells shared by lot and by turn.

zones.name_en: the swell at Cnoc chaol (LE 724) and the floods of Cuan dhearg
zones.note: A great swell with no storm took two children; An Gàire Dubh and a second flood at Cuan dhearg.
The houses divided four to three between Iain Ciar and Alasdair Bàn.
No living oak felled without the reeve's mark in every shire with a Doire in its name.

zones.name_en: the salt country of Ros fhionn (LE 354–1,179)
zones.note: Ros fhionn salt the common measure of worth in the north-eastern shires.

zones.name_en: the lordship of Seann Chwen for life (LE 1,276–1,291)
zones.note: Given to Alasdair Bàn at the brothers' peace; returned to the crown at his death.

the cold way of the grain barges (laid up LE 1,634)

hosts.name_en: the crown's riders on the coal-roads
hosts.note: Fresh horses at the waypoint houses; a rider carries the council's word to the mountain between dawn and dark. No standing host: the houses fight with their followings when they fight.

campaigns.name_en: the War of the Three Claimants
sides: Catrìona nic Aonghais of Inis thais
Dùghall Garbh of Baile Mòr dhomhain
Raghnall Ruadh, master of the vein-house
campaigns.outcome: Catrìona Bhuadhach crowned; the ruling of the hearth
boats burned on Eilean dhubh; Uilleam Ruadh hanged

campaigns.name: Cogadh nam Bràithrean
campaigns.outcome: peace at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr; Iain Ciar crowned

arms.blazon: Azure trellised Or, a fess cotised argent, over all a mascle argent.
arms.note: The vein-house's seal, a trellis of gold on blue (the galleries) with a hollow lozenge (Crom's slab), sealed on the king's letters from the joining; the crown added only the white band. The arms of the kingdom still.

arms.blazon: Azure trellised Or, over all a mascle argent (the custody's seal, without the crown's band).
arms.note: The seven houses sealed with the custody's seal; if they had badges of their own no roll remembers them.

polities.realm: Since the Sundering took one household in five across the water, the realm has been ruled by the seven houses of custody and the crown they make, and since Dòmhnall Ruadh the ruler has been master of the vein-house too. For nine centuries one hand has held both the vein and the realm, and the Small-Burning Law has not changed. At the close of the age the crown is empty and the Council of Custodians sits in its place.

burgs.489: Seann Skell of the west: the roll of the willing, the first keel, the sunwise turn in the river pool, and the quay renamed Cidhe an Diosail; now the seat of Manannan's order, whose priests pray the sea shut.
burgs.491: Muileann dhearg: the vein-house above the town, where Crom's stone and the custody-book are kept and the lots for the galleries were drawn.
burgs.23: Cathair mhòr: the greatest town on the island, the market of the south, and Macha's great house with its black and white floor.
burgs.19: Cathair dhearg: the crown's seat and the council's, smaller than its southern neighbour.
burgs.166: Inis thais: the first temple of Lia Fàil, and the town that gave the island Catrìona Bhuadhach.

rites.name: An Tùrsa Geal
rites.note: Undyed wool and an empty place at a meal that is neither feast nor fast; kept in every harbour town.

rites.name_en: the rite of the empty harbour, on Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell
rites.note: Kept by eleven people in LE 1,803; Manannan's priests say their prayer for the shut sea on the same day.

province_polity_notes.realm: One realm over every shire. The windy coast (no shire) has no hearth of the realm on record; the north-west shore is thinly held since the dearth (LE 819).
